analyzed_vuln.description: Heap-buffer-overflow read occurs because getMessageLength() unconditionally reads handshake header field length2 (be16toh(handshakeLayer->length2)) from m_Data without first ensuring m_DataLen >= sizeof(ssl_tls_handshake_layer). In this PoV, SSLHandshakeLayer::SSLHandshakeLayer() keeps parsing messages and calls message->getMessageLength() on a trailing truncated handshake fragment; createHandshakeMessage() accepted it as a message, then getMessageLength() reads past the end of the packet buffer by 2 bytes.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: FuzzTarget feeds a malformed TCP payload recognized as SSL handshake. In SSLHandshakeLayer::SSLHandshakeLayer (PcapPlusPlus/Packet++/src/SSLLayer.cpp), loop calls createHandshakeMessage(curPos, recordDataLen-curPosIndex, ...), then immediately calls getMessageLength() twice to advance. When remaining bytes at curPos are less than a full ssl_tls_handshake_layer (or otherwise truncated at buffer end), getMessageLength() still dereferences length2, causing OOB read at end of heap packet buffer. Trigger requires crafted SSL record/handshake lengths so parser reaches a final incomplete handshake message.
